findings.recommendation: Every new organization-scoped endpoint calls AuthorizeAsync first, decides before reading the target resource, declares OrgActionAttribute, and adds its action (and any new resource type) to OrgAction/OrgResource, the role table, the contract's fenced table and endpoint table, updating the contract test's count and resource pins. Keep scoped endpoints under /api/v1/organizations/{organizationId} or extend IsScoped. Gate UI on the permissions list from GET /organizations/{id}. Adding a built-in role needs maintainer approval (Q1). Which role holds a new action is that spec's clarification question.

findings.title: Database-layer posture for later role-gated writes and reads is undecided: Q3 = B covered GOZ-0004's admin-only writes only
evidence: src/Gozleme.Api/Persistence/Migrations/20261118000000_ScopedRbac.cs: organizations_update and invitations_insert/update/delete admit admins through gozleme.account_is_admin(org); memberships_guard requires admin for role changes, removals and adding others; reads stay member-level

docs/specs/004-scoped-rbac/progress.yaml decision rls-role-posture (Q3 option B): 'row-level rules and guards restrict every admin-only write (rename, invitation writes, removal of other members, role changes) to admins of that organization'

GOZ-0005 (publisher), GOZ-0014 (overlay writes), GOZ-0021 (review/approval), GOZ-0034 (grants) and GOZ-0012 (role-dependent visibility) will add role-gated actions on new tenant tables; the GOZ-0003-IF-01 default policy shape is member-level
GOZ-0018 policy conditions and facts cannot in general be expressed in SQL policies; only the role component can be mirrored
affectedSpecs: every spec adding a role-gated action on a tenant table
findings.recommendation: Maintainer decides before the GOZ-0005 plan. Option A: every later role-gated write (not reads) is also enforced in the database through a non-definer generalisation such as gozleme.account_has_role(org, role), following account_is_admin, with an isolation-matrix test per role; policy conditions from GOZ-0018 stay application-only. Option B: the database stays member-level for later tables; the role and policy decision is application-only and the PR states it as a known limitation (only GOZ-0004's admin writes are mirrored). Option C: decide per spec during each spec's clarification. In every option reads stay member-level in the database unless decided otherwise.
findings.disposition: human-decided 2026-11-16: option A (applied to future prompts)

decision.summary: Every later role-gated write is also enforced in the database, mirroring Q3 = B, via a non-definer SQL function account_has_role(org, role) that generalises account_is_admin. Reads stay member-level at the database. GOZ-0018 conditions stay application-only. The first consumer (expected GOZ-0005) adds the function and designs per-table policy shapes.

src/Gozleme.Api/Persistence/Migrations/20261118000000_ScopedRbac.cs: existing rows got {admin,member} via the temporary default, then the default is {member}; memberships_insert allows creators roles <@ {admin,member} and redeemers exactly {member}
memberships_guard binds the owner and superusers; GOZ-0003-IF-03 decision forbids disabling a guard in a migration, so no migration can assign roles

OrganizationEndpoints.SetRolesAsync: an admin may change any member's roles including its own (contracts/permissions.md 'raise own roles: refused (an own-row change is still a role change and needs admin)'; RoleAssignmentTests:115 a member cannot raise its own roles; :229 an admin changes its own roles); roles are not mutually exclusive; audit 1302 records before/after
OrganizationEndpoints.SetRolesAsync: losing admin revokes the account's open invitations in the same transaction (Q2 = A), the precedent for role-loss consequences
findings.recommendation: GOZ-0005 and GOZ-0021 state that nobody holds the new role after upgrade and an admin assigns it. Any creator default or backfill changes GOZ-0004's initial-role rule, so ask the maintainer. Each decides role-loss consequences for in-flight work explicitly and re-reads roles under the per-organization lock at decision time. GOZ-0021 enforces separation of duties between accounts per decision, and raises with the maintainer whether role combinations or self-grants should be forbidden. Seeded demo roles are assigned through the seeded admin.

findings.title: Row locks under role-restricted UPDATE policies silently lock nothing; lock order and the membership advisory lock
evidence: docs/specs/004-scoped-rbac/research.md R5: with organizations_update admin-only, a non-admin's SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on its organization returns zero rows and locks nothing

OrganizationEndpoints.LockMembersAsync takes gozleme.lock_organization_members(org) first and the organization row lock only for an admin caller; order advisory -> organization -> invitation; redemption takes organization (FOR KEY SHARE) -> invitation
OrganizationEndpoints.RevokeOpenInvitationsAsync relies on 'a non-admin never holds an open invitation' (Q2), asserted by a test
findings.recommendation: Use gozleme.lock_organization_members (or a new advisory lock in the same order) for per-organization serialization; never rely on a row lock on a table whose UPDATE policy may hide the row from the caller. Keep the lock order or prove a new one deadlock-free. A spec that gives invitation.create to a non-admin role must extend revocation on role loss.

findings.title: Known residual: deleting an account cascades its memberships past both the last-member and last-admin rules, and nothing can restore an admin
evidence: memberships_guard returns early for 'rls_internal() AND pg_trigger_depth() > 1' (FK cascades), research.md R4 'Consequence documented'
research.md R13: account deletion, HTTP recovery and platform administrator are not built; gozleme_app's DELETE on users is GOZ-0001/0003 posture
Role changes need an admin (memberships_guard, membership.roles.change admin-only), so an admin-less organization cannot be repaired through the product
findings.recommendation: Whichever spec first adds account deletion, erasure or account merging defines the last-admin and last-member behaviour first (for example, refuse to delete a last admin, or require a handover). An operator recovery command would be new scope for the maintainer. No change is needed in GOZ-0004.

findings.title: GOZ-0039 restore and release gate must account for guard triggers
evidence: memberships_guard and invitations_guard are BEFORE triggers with no signed context bypass; with no context current_account_id() is null, so an inserted membership for another account requires account_is_admin and is refused
pg_dump places trigger creation in post-data, so a full restore loads rows before the trigger exists; a data-only restore into an existing schema fires the guard
RlsCatalog does not inspect triggers (GOZ-0003-IF-19); guards are proved only by behavioural tests (RbacIsolationTests, TenantContextBoundaryTests)
findings.recommendation: Restore procedure uses a full restore or superuser --disable-triggers under the GOZ-0003-IF-11 procedure. The release gate verifies that memberships_guard and invitations_guard exist and are enabled, and that the permission contract, RBAC isolation and role tests pass.

findings.title: Implementation defect: any member can set another member's invitation_id to NULL at the database layer
evidence: src/Gozleme.Api/Persistence/Migrations/20261118000000_ScopedRbac.cs memberships_guard: the identity check refuses invitation_id changes only when NEW.invitation_id IS NOT NULL, and an update with unchanged roles returns before the admin check; memberships_update admits every row of the caller's organizations

Reproduced on the running stack at 7179977, inside a rolled-back transaction: as gozleme_app in carol's signed context (account_is_admin = false), UPDATE gozleme.memberships SET invitation_id = NULL on alice's row in Seeded Demo Org changed 1 row. A follow-up read confirmed no change persisted

The FK ON DELETE SET NULL cascade already passes through the 'rls_internal() AND pg_trigger_depth() > 1' branch, so the depth-1 NULL allowance is not needed for it; no application path sets InvitationId except redemption
RbacIsolationTests covers only setting invitation_id to a new value (refused)

Fixed on the branch before the PR: memberships_guard now refuses any direct invitation_id change (the FK SET NULL cascade passes at pg_trigger_depth() > 1); RbacIsolationTests asserts a member nulling its own or a co-member's invitation_id, and an admin nulling a member's, are refused with 42501; make test 318/318, make demo 41 passed after make reset
findings.recommendation: Bounded correction for drive-speckit: refuse any invitation_id change at depth 1 (the cascade branch already covers SET NULL), add a RbacIsolationTests case where a member nulls a co-member's and its own invitation_id, keep the research.md R4 step 3 text in sync, then re-run convergence and this analysis. Impact is limited to the redemption provenance link (invitations.used_by still records it), so the maintainer may instead accept it as a documented residual.
